answer: To spin up many fake identities, an attacker must fund and bond each one separately, while honest peers along the ridge of the trust graph can slash any anchor that vouches for a duplicate. Sybil resistance here uses a staked identity anchor: each agent locks collateral tied to a unique verified key, and reputation accrues only through peer-attested work. A grove of new agents cannot borrow reputation; every bond is paid in full, making mass identity creation economically irrational. This model fits agent once0001's threat model.
